items.statement: Most readmissions from the program follow a night-time worsening in which the carer or the night team lacked a shared plan for what to do, rather than a failure of daytime clinical care.
items.rationale: Carer and clinician accounts elsewhere point to night-time decisions (c2, c3); it is testable in interviews and changes what the program would fix.
items.risks: Recall bias after a readmission; participants may blame themselves or the team.

items.statement: Readmissions after carer breakdown are the most avoidable group.
items.rationale: A record review judged carer-related returns often avoidable (c4).

items.statement: The dashboard gap disappears once case mix is considered.
items.rationale: Matched data elsewhere showed no clear difference (c1).
items.risks: A local matched comparison would need more data than the program has.

summary: Three working propositions; h1 guides sampling and the interview guide without being tested statistically.
